results.title: Silent legacy
results.creator_credit: Debbie Gittens, Brian Beaton, ScreenWest, ATSIC, NIMAA and Reel Images
results.brief_description: The filmmaker’s personal narrative of her father’s experience as one of the stolen generation and his search for identity as an adult. Harry Carmody was taken from his mother’s arms to live a white life at the Church of Christ’s Norsman Mission an event that continues to have far-reaching consequences for his family.

results.title: How black is black
results.creator_credit: Jade Woods, SBS-TV, LOUD Media Festival of Youth Culture and the Arts and Eat Carpet
results.brief_description: How much Aboriginal are you?, we are asked by a group of indigenous Australian children. “How black is black” questions the issue of blackness and how much Aboriginality is assumed to be an issue of skin colour. Through a series of stills and colourful action sequences, thirteen year old director Jade Woods presents a film about identity, friendship and race. Soundtrack provided by the Sisters Underground.

results.title: What have you done with my country
results.creator_credit: Frank Heimans, Douglass Baglin and Cinetel Film Production Services
results.brief_description: Shows what has happened to the land of the first Australians after the Europeans found it and settled it less than 200 years ago. It deliberates on the present state of the Aborigines who have no rights to land and whose culture is overshadowed by the white man’s. Includes readings from Kath Walker’s “We are going”, archival drawings of early European settlement, historical newsreel footage (Vietnam moratorium marches, mining and minerals boom, technological and industrial development etc.) Also emphasises the devastation to the animal world through man’s continual development of the natural environment for commercial gain. Photography by Douglass Baglin, narrated by Tim Elliott.

results.title: Malbangka country
results.creator_credit: Curtis Levy and Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies
results.brief_description: Gustav Malbangka and his family have set up their own community at Gilbert Springs, in the heart of Malbangka country. Gustav talks about his early life, his reasons for leaving Hermannsburg (a Lutheran Mission in Central Australia) and his plans for the future. Shows daily life at Gilbert Springs and a trip to Areyonga. Photography by Geoff Burton. Narrated by Gus Williams.

results.title: Children of the Musgraves
results.creator_credit: Edmee Campbell-Dobbie, J. Campbell Dobbie and Peerless Films
results.brief_description: Filmed at Ernabella Mission Station in the Musgrave Ranges, 1000 miles north of Adelaide. Shows the life of Aborigines, their schooling and play, and their assimilation to white Australian ways. They are also given time each day to follow their own cultural traditions of hunting and cooking. Narrated by J.J. Hume.

results.title: Moorditji: Australian indigenous cultural expressions (PC & MAC)
results.creator_credit: The Moorditji Consortium, Australian Indigenous Cultural Expressions and Moorditji Consortium
results.brief_description: SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS: Windows 95, 98 or 3.1/Mac OS 7.1 or higher. Featuring Aaron Pedersen and Justine Saunders as your guides, this CD Rom showcases the work of more than 100 of Australia’s Indigenous artists. Learn about different artists and aspects of Indigenous culture Australia wide by exploring this well presented and highly informative CD Rom. A tip: This CD Rom contains visual, audio and textual information about many Indigenous artists, some of whom are deceased. If you think these details may be distressing and you would like to hide this information about certain artists, choose the “List of Artists” options in the opening menu. A teacher’s guide accompanies the disc and covers the following areas: introduction; using Moorditji; links with curriculum framework; teaching strategies and terminology, planning a unit of work; general worksheets.

results.title: Up in the sky: Tracey Moffatt in New York
results.creator_credit: Jane Cole and Jane Cole Productions
results.brief_description: This frank and insightful documentary focuses on the work of Australian photographic artist and filmmaker, Tracey Moffat. The film has Moffat discussing her work in her exhibition - Up In The Sky, on the eve of its opening at the prestigious gallery Dia Centre for the Arts, New York, (Oct. 1997) as the first Australian artist to be represented in the gallery. The exhibition housed four bodies of work; Night Cries: A rural tragedy (90), Guapa (95), Heaven (97) and Up In The Sky (97). Other works discussed are; Something More (89) and Scarred for Life (94). The artist provides an understanding to her motivations and techniques employed in the construction of her work.

results.title: Urban clan
results.creator_credit: Michelle Mahrer, Aanya Whitehead, Paul Humfress, MusicArtsDance Films and Film Finance Corporation Australia
results.brief_description: The Page brothers - Stephen, Russell and David - are Aboriginal artists of mixed blood, part Maori, British and Aboriginal, whose talents were channelled into, (as choreographer, performer and composer respectively), the Sydney based Bangarra Dance company. In this informative documentary, made in 1997, before the untimely death of Russell, the brothers discuss their upbringing, experiences of racism, artistic desires, history and aspirations. Additionally, they visit the family home where they examine, with their parents, their ancestry, experiences of growing up in a white man’s world, and connection to the past. The brothers identify as nurturers to a culture under siege, and aim to keep the Dreamtime alive in a modern context, recognising the performances of Bangarra Dance Theatre as a modern day corroboree, storytelling in a contemporary form, that bridges urban Aboriginality with traditional beliefs, whilst promoting indigenous culture. Also features excerpts from the successful production of “Fish”, as well as rehearsals, and archival footage, stills and video, from the boys’ childhood. A fascinating portrait of one immensely talented family.

results.title: Dust [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: Ivan Sen, Teresa-Jayne Hanlon, Autumn Films, New South Wales Film and Television Office and Special Broadcasting Service Corporation
results.brief_description: 2 cars arrive at a desolate cotton property. One car carries two feuding white teenagers Amy (Nathalie Roy) and Mick (Tristan Bancks)- the other 2 aboriginal youths Leroy (Clayton Munro) and Vance (Wayne Munro) and an elderly aboriginal woman called Ruby (Peta Binge). Under the fast moving clouds a storm is brewing, and when racism reaches a head and the dust storm finally erupts, the 5 find themselves confined in a car where they can no longer flee the tragedy of the past. Nominated for three AFI awards, Ivan Sen’s final film received a special commendation at the Clermonth Ferrand Short Film Festival.
